Subject: Pilot pathway & latency/throughput breakdown for deployment mode

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — quick recap and a proposed next step so we can align on whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private is the right path for QuickCart.

TL;DR from our call: you have two operating windows — normal traffic (~60 qps sustained) and peak flash-sales (~up to 400 qps for 3–5 minute bursts). The engineering team called out an end-to-end inference SLO of P95 <= 150 ms (user-facing) for your recommendation API. Data residency is US-only for logs, but request payloads are not regulated.

What I captured as key constraints:
- Typical sustained concurrency: 40–70 qps (spikes infrequently).
- Planned flash peaks: up to ~400 qps for short bursts (3–10 minutes).
- Latency target: P95 <= 150 ms (end-to-end server-side).
- Context window: up to 256 tokens; typical response length ~40 tokens.
- Security: standard SOC2 controls, no additional legal constraints today.

Initial recommendation (call follow-up):
- Pilot on Hosted API first to validate functional correctness and latency under normal load. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and we can instrument p95 metrics quickly.
- For flash peak protection and predictable cost, plan a Dedicated capacity evaluation: a reserved GPU pool with burst capacity and autoscale to cover the 400 qps bursts while keeping P95 below 150 ms.
- If you want strict isolation or on-prem requirements later, we can scope a Private VPC pilot, but that looks unnecessary based on current answers.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick smoke pilot on Hosted (2 weeks) to capture baseline p50/p95 and token-cost profile.
2) If p95 under Hosted is >150 ms at normal load, we either: tweak batching/caching and repeat, or move to Dedicated for predictable headroom.
3) Run a Dedicated sizing exercise (we can run load tests) to validate a 1-hour cost projection and latency SLO under 400 qps bursts.

I've attached a short options summary and a mutual action plan template. If you confirm the numbers above are accurate, I'll schedule the Hosted smoke pilot to start next week and loop in our SRE for a coordinated load test.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15 min sync to finalize dates.

—Marcus

Looping in my recommendations from the sizing perspective so Marcus can reply to Aisha with concrete next steps.

Summary of sizing logic:
- Hosted API: good for functional validation and sustained ~60 qps. We should instrument request-level timing and token counts (we can add an SDK hook to surface model-side p50/p95). Expect Hosted p95 for this workload: ~80–220 ms depending on model variant and batching behavior. If their observed p95 is <150 ms on Hosted at normal load, Hosted pilot is sufficient to validate product fit.

- Dedicated capacity: recommended if QuickCart needs consistent P95 <=150 ms during the 400 qps spike. For the 256-token context and ~40-token outputs, our sizing model suggests a Dedicated GPU pool (N x A100-style or equivalent) with continuous batching window tuned to their qps distribution and a short-request-priority lane for low-latency singletons.

- Cost trade-offs: very roughly, Hosted + burst protection (on-demand reserved scaling) can be 20–40% cheaper for low sustained qps but may experience higher p95 during spikes. Dedicated reservations reduce per-token cost at high sustained throughput and give predictable tail latency. We'll produce a three-scenario cost appendix (Normal, Peak, Combined) for QCR to review.

Operational asks for the pilot:
- We own Hosted pilot instrumentation + load test. QuickCart to grant a small list of test IPs and a service account key for the test harness.
- If pilot shows p95 breach during spikes, we move to a short Dedicated POC: 72-hour burst test on reserved capacity with our autoscaler settings.

I'll draft a short message to Aisha with dates and attach a quick cost appendix (estimate).

—Marissa
